books.title: Aesop’s Fables
books.author: Aesop, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones
books.blurb: Short animal stories that each end with a lesson: the hare and the tortoise, the lion and the mouse, the boy who cried wolf, and more.

books.title: Around the World in Eighty Days: Retold
books.author: Jules Verne
books.blurb: Phileas Fogg bets half his fortune that he can race round the world in eighty days. With his loyal servant Passepartout, and a detective hot on their heels, he crosses the world by steamship, train, elephant and a sledge with sails, right down to the very last second.

books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.blurb: Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr. Darcy get each other completely wrong.

books.title: The Age of Fable: Stories of Gods and Heroes
books.author: Thomas Bulfinch
books.blurb: The Greek and Roman myths retold for readers of poetry: Prometheus, Proserpine, Theseus, the Golden Fleece, the fall of Troy and the wanderings of Ulysses and Aeneas (Bulfinch uses the Roman names).

books.title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.blurb: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole into a world of mad tea-parties, a grinning cat and a furious Queen.

books.title: A Christmas Carol
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.blurb: On Christmas Eve the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by his dead partner’s ghost, and by three spirits.

books.title: A Tale of Two Cities
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.blurb: London and Paris before and during the French Revolution: a prisoner recalled to life, a family in danger, and a great sacrifice.

books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: Eight of the great detective’s cases, told by his friend Dr. Watson: a league of red-headed men, a goose with a jewel inside it, and a whistle in the night.

books.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: A legend of a spectral hound, a death on Dartmoor, and Holmes and Watson’s most famous case.

books.title: The Wind in the Willows
books.author: Kenneth Grahame
books.blurb: Mole, Ratty and Badger mess about on the river, and try to save the boastful, motor-car-mad Toad from himself.

books.title: Sherlock Holmes and the Blue Carbuncle
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: Cases for Young Detectives. At Christmas, a battered old hat and a fat goose are found in a London street, and inside the goose is a stolen jewel. Sherlock Holmes follows the trail of the goose across frosty London to catch the real thief.

books.title: Sherlock Holmes and the Norwood Builder
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: Cases for Young Detectives. A builder vanishes on the night he leaves his fortune to a young lawyer, and the police are sure the lawyer is to blame. Then a thumbprint appears on the wall, and Sherlock Holmes starts to laugh.

books.title: Sherlock Holmes and the Red-Headed League
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: Cases for Young Detectives. Why would anyone pay a red-haired shopkeeper four pounds a week to copy out an encyclopedia? Sherlock Holmes studies the knees of a young man’s trousers and uncovers a secret tunnel heading for a cellar full of gold.

books.title: Sherlock Holmes and Silver Blaze
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: Cases for Young Detectives. The fastest racehorse in England vanishes a week before the big race, and his trainer is found hurt on the moor. Can Sherlock Holmes find Silver Blaze in time, and what does the dog that did nothing in the night-time have to do with it?

books.title: The Odyssey
books.author: Homer, translated by William Cullen Bryant
books.blurb: Odysseus’s ten-year voyage home from Troy, past the Cyclops, Circe and the Sirens, while suitors crowd his palace. In flowing blank verse.

books.title: Just So Stories
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.blurb: How did the elephant get his trunk, and the camel his hump? Kipling’s funny, sing-song stories for his “Best Beloved”, best read aloud.

books.title: The Railway Children
books.author: E. Nesbit
books.blurb: When Father is taken away, Roberta, Peter and Phyllis move to a cottage by the railway, wave to the trains, and save one from disaster.

books.title: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.blurb: Peter’s cousin Benjamin takes him back into the garden to fetch his lost clothes, and they meet the cat.

books.title: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.blurb: Jemima wants to hatch her own eggs, and a very polite gentleman with sandy whiskers offers her a place to nest.

books.title: More Tales from Beatrix Potter
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.blurb: Seven more little books: two naughty mice in a doll’s house, a hedgehog washerwoman, a frog who goes fishing, and more (1904–1918).

books.title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.blurb: Peter squeezes under the gate into Mr. McGregor’s garden, though his mother told him not to. Can he get out again?

books.title: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.blurb: Cheeky Nutkin teases Old Brown the owl with riddles. Can you solve them before he does?

books.title: Black Beauty
books.author: Anna Sewell
books.blurb: A horse tells his own life story, from a happy country childhood to hard years pulling a London cab.

books.title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
books.author: Mary Shelley
books.blurb: A young scientist gives life to a creature he has built, then abandons it. Told in letters from an Arctic expedition.

books.title: Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.blurb: The lawyer Utterson wants to know why his respectable friend Dr. Jekyll has left everything to the brutal Mr. Hyde.

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.blurb: Young Jim Hawkins finds a pirate’s map and sails for buried treasure, with the one-legged sea-cook Long John Silver aboard.

books.title: The War of the Worlds
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.blurb: A cylinder lands on Horsell Common, and the Martians inside begin their conquest of Surrey and London.

books.title: The Selfish Giant and Other Tales
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.blurb: A giant who shuts the children out of his garden, a rocket who thinks he is the most important firework in the world, and more fairy tales to share.
